description:
FILED s473t6d (Opus, 2026-09-20) by #1501 round 11 (CHECK 1 on t/op/lex.t's
one-row shortfall).

REPRODUCER (perl 5.40.3 prints `rhubarb`; PCL drops the statement):

    $_ = "rhubarb";
    print ${no strict; \$_}, "\n";

PCL:

    PCL: statement not supported at t/op/lex.t line 99:
      is ${no strict; \$_}, "rhubarb", '${no strict; ...}';
      -- Bug. Fell through. Missing case:
         ['Statement::Include<no strict;>','Statement<\$_>']

`${ BLOCK }` is perl's block form of the scalar dereference, and its BLOCK is
an ordinary block: any number of statements, the LAST one's value being the
reference.  PCL's `${ â¦ }` lowering accepts a single expression, so a block
that opens with a pragma (or with any other statement) falls through to the
generic "missing case" and the whole statement is dropped -- a #138 drop that
aborts its top-level form.

ROWS: `baselines/perl-suite-fails.tsv` op/lex.t 9 `${no strict; ...}`, and the
file's whole 1-row shortfall (`baselines/row-shortfall.tsv t/op/lex.t`).

SHAPE: the same question `@{ BLOCK }` and `%{ BLOCK }` answer -- lower the
cast's Structure::Block as a BLOCK whose value is its last statement, rather
than as a single expression.  Check the sibling casts before adding an arm to
`$` alone (rule 11).
subject: `${ no strict; EXPR }` -- a scalar-cast BLOCK whose body holds a pragma STATEMENT plus an expression -- is a #138 DROP
